newsitem.title: ITALY: Swiss-Italian accused of graft out on probation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss-Italian accused of graft out on probation.

text.p: A Swiss-Italian banker suspected of leading a major graft network was released from house arrest in Italy on Friday and placed on probation.

A magistrate in the central town of Perugia ruled that Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia, 62, for reasons of poor health and age, need not be confined to his house provided he lived at his home near Pisa and did not travel abroad.
"Freedom is a great gift," Pacini Battaglia's lawyer quoted him as saying on hearing the news.
Pacini Battaglia was arrested last September along with the former head of the state railway, Lorenzo Necci. He was put under house arrest earlier this month while Necci was set free.
Neither has yet been charged, but commentators say inquiries into their activities have revealed a "superlobby" of businessmen, judges and lawyers operating across a swathe of state sectors.
